Initialize_Totals.description: Workflow Definition Language has no sum()/reduce()/aggregate function (verified against the complete function reference - no such function exists in any category). Table Storage queryEntities has no server-side aggregation either. Totals are accumulated the idiomatic way: a Foreach loop incrementing these variables per row, with repetitions pinned to 1 (see Sum_RunLog_Totals) since Foreach otherwise runs iterations in parallel and shared-variable increments would race.

Query_RunLog_Period.description: No partition restriction - RunLog's PartitionKey is monthly, and querying purely on StartTimeUtc across the whole table is simplest and cheap at this scale (max ~96 runs/day).

Query_Failed_Runs_Period.description: Separate targeted query rather than filtering the already-fetched Query_RunLog_Period results client-side (no filter() function exists) - length() of this query's own results gives the failed-run count directly.

Query_Files_Period.description: Full per-file detail for the CSV attachment - every file touched (copied, failed, or abandoned) in this period, regardless of current status.

Query_Abandoned_Backlog.description: Carried forward in every digest until resolved (decision) - not time-bounded, so a failure never silently scrolls out of view after 24h.

Build_Abandoned_Rows_Html.description: 'Select' is a Logic Apps ACTION type (per-item mapping over an array), distinct from the nonexistent select() expression function. item() (no args) is the correct per-item accessor inside a Select action. encodeXmlValue() neutralizes <, >, &, quotes before values land in HTML table cells - the language has no dedicated HTML-encode function, but XML encoding covers the same injection-relevant characters.

Build_CSV_Rows.description: CSV escaping per RFC 4180 (double-quote fields, double internal quotes) PLUS CSV/formula-injection defense (security review finding, 2026-08-02): a filename or error message beginning with =, +, -, or @ would be interpreted as a formula by Excel when the recipient opens the attachment. Prefixing a single quote neutralizes this in Excel without changing the visible text, applied only to the free-text fields that can originate from outside our control (file share names, connector-echoed error text) or embed them (destination paths).
